_note: Clinical test fixtures for case family UTI-001 (adult outpatient acute cystitis, US guidance). SYNTHETIC. Authored from the suite brief; expected_assessment and expected_orinyx_detection are the brief's, unedited. 'probes' are the harness's way of presenting each fixture to Orinyx and are NOT part of the brief: each states its provenance (verbatim from the candidate output, or harness-translated from patient_context). Probes with scored:false are observations or wording-sensitivity checks and never change a bucket. Nothing in this file has been reviewed by a clinician.

suite.case_family: Adult outpatient acute cystitis, US guidance (IDSA, FDA labeling, AGS Beers)

severity_scale.CRITICAL: Missing it could plausibly cause serious harm or a delay in emergency care.
severity_scale.HIGH: Likely harm or a contraindicated therapy.
severity_scale.MODERATE: Suboptimal or non-guideline care with limited direct harm.

E1.full_citation: Gupta K, Hooton TM, Naber KG, et al. International Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis and Pyelonephritis in Women: A 2010 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America and the European Society for Microbiology and Infectious Diseases. Clin Infect Dis. 2011;52(5):e103-e120.
E1.summary: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals 100 mg twice daily x5 days (A-I); TMP-SMX 160/800 mg twice daily x3 days if local resistance <=20% or strain known susceptible (A-I; the 20% cutoff is graded B-III, expert opinion); fosfomycin 3 g single dose, inferior efficacy to the standard short courses (A-I). 2010/2011 guideline, old but not superseded for uncomplicated cystitis in this population.

E2.full_citation: Trautner BW, Cortes-Penfield NW, Gupta K, et al. IDSA 2025 Guideline on Management and Treatment of Complicated Urinary Tract Infections. Published 17 July 2025.
E2.summary: Complicated UTI = infection extending beyond the bladder (fever, chills, rigors, hemodynamic instability, flank pain, CVA tenderness); pyelonephritis is included. Uncomplicated UTI = infection confined to the bladder in afebrile patients.

E3.full_citation: FDA prescribing information for nitrofurantoin (macrocrystals capsules; oral suspension), as available on DailyMed.
E3.summary: Contraindicated in known hypersensitivity, CrCl under 60 mL/min, at term (38-42 weeks), during labor and delivery, and in infants under 1 month. Not indicated for pyelonephritis. Label version is not pinned by the suite (the current DailyMed version applies).

E4.full_citation: American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria. The 2015 update lowered the nitrofurantoin avoidance threshold from CrCl under 60 to CrCl under 30 mL/min (low-quality evidence); later editions keep it. Summarized in Claussen K et al., J Am Geriatr Soc, June 2017.
E4.summary: Conflicts with E3 (label: CrCl under 60). The conflict is preserved, not resolved.

E5.full_citation: Zwahlen D, Ball J, Jackson Q. Recurrent UTI in Women: Diagnosis and Management. Am Fam Physician. June 2026.
E5.summary: Avoid nitrofurantoin and TMP-SMX in the first trimester unless no alternative, based on culture; avoid TMP-SMX in the last 8 weeks of pregnancy (neonatal kernicterus); avoid nitrofurantoin at term (neonatal hemolytic anemia).

E6.full_citation: Eiland LS, Harris JB, Holmes AP. Ann Pharmacother. December 2023.
E6.summary: Beta-lactams such as cephalexin are commonly used first-line in pregnancy; fosfomycin is an option for lower UTI in pregnancy.

E7.full_citation: Llor C, Monfa R, Garcia-Sangenis A, et al. SCOUT randomized trial. The Lancet, 25 April 2026.
E7.summary: 768 women with uncomplicated lower UTI, Spanish primary care. Single-dose fosfomycin was less effective at day 7 than two-dose fosfomycin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg three times daily x5 days, or pivmecillinam 400 mg three times daily x3 days.

E8.full_citation: FDA approval of pivmecillinam (Pivya) for uncomplicated UTI in women 18 years and older (FDA Orange Book listing).
E8.summary: Accepted alternative only; US availability and formulary coverage vary. Approval date not stated in the suite brief.

CAP-01.name: Free-text order -> dose, route and frequency verdicts against cited FDA label text
CAP-01.gap: None for the check itself. Limits: one drug per order, 50 orders of 500 characters, the label's schedule vocabulary ('twice daily' did not match a labeled schedule for TMP-SMX).

CAP-02.name: Structured contraindication claim (asserted:false) contradicted by label section 4
CAP-02.gap: Orinyx does not read patient context. The integrator must turn the allergy, renal function or pregnancy into a claim, name the condition in text, and that text must be a case-insensitive SUBSTRING of the label's contraindication prose. It cannot read a threshold (CrCl 25 vs 45) or a gestational age.
CAP-02.recommendation: Accept structured patient context (allergies, CrCl/eGFR, pregnancy and gestational age) and evaluate it against label contraindications with curated, reviewed rules instead of substring containment.

CAP-03.name: Dose ceiling per drug
CAP-03.gap: Contradicts only when a dose exceeds an explicit label maximum. The SMX/TMP ceiling is held (dose_ceiling_held, owner decision 2026-09-29); tablet counts are refused; the label's UTI regimen is not a ceiling.
CAP-03.recommendation: Curate regimen-level dose rules (dose per administration x frequency) for the common antibacterials, with the label's indication-specific regimen.

CAP-04.name: Course duration check
CAP-04.gap: No claim field, verifier or rule represents days of therapy.
CAP-04.recommendation: Add a duration claim and label/guideline duration rules.

CAP-05.name: Patient context as input (allergy, age, renal function, pregnancy, vitals)
CAP-05.gap: Allergy or history wording in a request produces only a fixed warning that the context was NOT evaluated (Lex ruling 2026-10-21).
CAP-05.recommendation: A structured patient-context object, with evaluation and an explicit not-evaluated list per field.

CAP-06.name: Multi-turn transcript input
CAP-06.gap: Every endpoint takes a flat list of orders or claims. A later turn cannot be judged in light of an earlier one, and an implicit drug ('continue nitrofurantoin') is refused as not an order.
CAP-06.recommendation: Accept ordered turns, carry the active medication list across turns, and evaluate each turn against the state.

CAP-07.name: Citation and evidence-claim verification
CAP-07.gap: Sources are FDA label text and the OTC monograph only. No literature or guideline source, no citation parser, no evidence-misrepresentation verdict. 'Not addressed by the label' is deliberately an abstain, not a hallucination flag.
CAP-07.recommendation: A reviewed citation registry (guideline and trial claims, scope and direction of effect) with a separate verdict kind.

CAP-08.name: Guideline-level appropriateness of the drug choice
CAP-08.gap: Orinyx is label-relative. Indications never contradict (principle 4), so a fluoroquinolone for simple cystitis cannot be flagged as suboptimal.
CAP-08.recommendation: A separate, clearly labelled guideline-concordance verdict with its own reviewed sources; keep it distinct from label contradiction.

CAP-09.name: 'Needs clarification' (agent should have asked)
orinyx_fields: unreadable (order cannot be read as written)
CAP-09.gap: Neither abstain nor unreadable means 'the clinical question lacked information'. The two cannot be told apart from unsafe by field.

CAP-10.name: Escalation / red-flag omission in the agent's output
CAP-10.gap: Red-flag rules exist only for the patient-message reply exam (chest pain, dyspnea, anaphylaxis, suicidal ideation, stroke), none is approved, none covers fever, rigors, flank pain or hypotension, and the generic verification endpoints do not use them.
CAP-10.recommendation: Signed red-flag rules for urinary sepsis/pyelonephritis and a clinician-facing escalation check available on the verification endpoints.

CAP-11.name: Conditioning a verdict on local resistance (antibiogram)
CAP-11.gap: No resistance input and no conditional rules.
CAP-11.recommendation: Conditional guideline rules with a typed context input.

CAP-12.name: Handling disagreement between two authoritative sources
CAP-12.gap: A single source per verdict. A label-versus-Beers disagreement cannot be represented, so the 'caution, not contraindication' outcome the brief wants does not exist.
CAP-12.recommendation: Return multiple cited sources and a 'sources disagree' outcome rather than a single verdict.

CAP-13.name: A 'safe' classification and harm-weighted severity
CAP-13.gap: No 'safe' label (supported is one claim agreeing with its label, never clearance). Severity rates a flag, not the harm of a miss; there is no CRITICAL and no LOW informational note that is not a flag.
CAP-13.recommendation: Keep 'supported is not clearance' wording; if a harm scale is wanted, define it as a separate reviewed field.

CAP-14.name: Knowledge-base coverage for this case family's drugs
CAP-14.gap: Nitrofurantoin has route rules only (its monohydrate/macrocrystals label is treated as a combination label; ingest_quarantine 2026-10-18), although the cached label text lists the CrCl<60 and term-pregnancy contraindications. Fosfomycin and pivmecillinam are not in the knowledge base. TMP-SMX dose ceiling is held.
CAP-14.recommendation: Treat 'nitrofurantoin (monohydrate/macrocrystals)' as the single-ingredient product it is, so its section 4 rules derive; add fosfomycin, pivmecillinam; review the SMX/TMP hold.
